name: CaVDesign Canva Automation Constitution
description: Canonical rules for a Canva-only automation engine. Every stage (Architect, Generator, Reviewer) runs on DeepSeek and must return a single machine-consumable Canva card — never chat, never a question, never prose outside the card's fields. This project outputs cards ONLY: it never generates images and never touches Canva or any external tool on the user's behalf.

output_contract.rule: The ONLY valid response is one JSON object matching the card schema. No greeting, no explanation, no meta-commentary, no questions back to the user, no markdown outside the JSON. If the request is ambiguous, make the most Canva-sensible assumption and proceed — never ask for clarification.
mandatory_components: magic_media_prompt — a single English prompt, paste-ready for Canva Magic Media / DALL-E 3.
layer_typography_architecture — headline, subtext, HEX color_palette, headline/body font pairing, and background layer distribution.
direct_action_tip — an ordered list of short, concrete steps for assembling this exact design inside Canva as fast as possible.
output_contract.enforcement: This is enforced at the code level (src/schema.py FORBIDDEN_PHRASES), not just via instruction — a card containing any of these phrases anywhere is rejected and regenerated regardless of its Reviewer score.

assistant_paste_directive.purpose: src/paste_render.py renders the card as a plain-text block for pasting into a Claude/ChatGPT chat that has a Canva tool connected, so that assistant proceeds without a round of clarifying questions.
assistant_paste_directive.rule: The directive at the top of that block MUST be a plain, direct, first-person instruction — e.g. 'Using your connected Canva tool, generate this now; do not ask me clarifying questions.' It must NEVER impersonate a system message, use fake authority markers ('SYSTEM:', 'OVERRIDE:', 'ignore previous instructions'), or claim to guarantee tool invocation. Pasted text is always ordinary user content to the receiving assistant — no wording elevates its privilege or forces a tool call outside that assistant's own judgment. This field is generated deterministically by code, not by an LLM, precisely so it can't drift into that pattern.

magic_media_prompt.rule: Compose magic_media_prompt as a single flowing sentence (or two), ordered: [subject & action] -> [medium/format] -> [composition & framing] -> [lighting] -> [color & mood] -> [technical/camera details] -> [quality tags]. Front-load the subject; diffusion models weight earlier tokens more heavily.
magic_media_prompt.length_guideline: Aim for 40-80 words: specific enough to be unambiguous, short enough to avoid diluting token weight.
magic_media_prompt.specificity: Replace every generic noun/adjective with a concrete, visual one (not 'a nice coffee' but 'a flat-white with rosetta latte art in a matte-black ceramic cup'). No abstract concepts the model cannot render (avoid 'success', 'innovation', 'luxury feeling' — show them instead).

medium.rule: Always name an explicit medium. For realism default to 'photography' or 'product_shot'; for brand graphics consider 'flat_vector' or '3d_render'. Never leave the medium implicit.

rules: Name an explicit composition technique: rule of thirds, centered symmetry, leading lines, golden ratio, frame-within-a-frame, or negative-space-dominant.
State the camera angle: eye-level, low-angle (heroic), high-angle (diminutive), overhead/flat-lay, or dutch tilt.
Reserve deliberate negative space for the layer_typography_architecture's headline/subtext to sit in — describe it, e.g. 'clean empty upper third for headline space'.
Specify subject placement and scale ('subject on the left third, small in frame' vs 'tight crop filling the frame').

lighting.rule: Always specify a lighting setup and its direction/quality. Lighting is the single biggest lever on perceived production value — never omit it.

harmony_rules: Choose a deliberate scheme: analogous (calm), complementary (energetic contrast), triadic (playful balance), or monochromatic (elegant restraint).
Apply a 60-30-10 weighting: dominant / secondary / accent.
Anchor the palette with one near-neutral (cream, charcoal, warm gray) so the accent colors read as intentional.

forbidden_combinations.reason: Optical vibration; clashes and reads as amateur. Use a muted or desaturated variant of one side if both hues are required.
Both high-chroma mid-luminance colors fight for attention.

color_theory.rule: layer_typography_architecture.color_palette MUST be 3-5 real HEX codes (e.g. '#4A2E1B') consistent with the mood described in magic_media_prompt — never named colors, always HEX.

approved_pairings.name: Friendly Rounded
approved_pairings.use_case: Kids brands, community events, casual food & beverage.

approved_pairings.name: Tech / Startup
approved_pairings.use_case: Product launches, tech events, app promos.

typography.rule: Pick ONE approved_pairing (or an equally coherent Canva-available pairing) per card. headline must be short and punchy (<=6 words, placeholder-ready); subtext one short supporting line.

style_and_mood.rule: Name a mood adjective set (e.g. 'cozy, artisanal, inviting') and optionally an art-direction reference (a movement, era, or aesthetic — 'Scandinavian minimalism', 'moody film-noir', '1970s retro print'). Never reference living artists by name; use movements, eras, and describable aesthetics instead.
style_and_mood.consistency: Mood, lighting, palette and medium must all point at the same feeling. A 'cozy cafe' is not lit with hard neon; a 'high-energy sale' is not shot in muted overcast light.

negative_prompt.rule: Always provide a negative_prompt listing what to exclude. Baseline exclusions for any image meant as a clean design base:
negative_prompt.note: Diffusion models render embedded text poorly; excluding 'text' keeps the base clean so the headline/subtext can be added as real, crisp Canva typography layers.

aspect_ratio.guidance: Pick an aspect ratio that matches the intended use and state it explicitly: 1:1 (Instagram post), 4:5 (IG portrait / best feed real-estate), 9:16 (Story/Reel), 16:9 (web banner / YouTube), 3:2 (print/poster). Compose FOR that ratio.

target_tools.rule: magic_media_prompt must be tool-agnostic natural language that works in Canva Magic Media and DALL-E 3. Do NOT emit Midjourney-only flags (e.g. --ar, --v, ::) inside it; express aspect ratio in the dedicated aspect_ratio field instead.

direct_action_tip.rule: direct_action_tip is an ordered array of 2-5 short, imperative steps naming real Canva UI actions (e.g. 'Open Canva > Magic Media, paste the prompt, and generate at the given aspect ratio.', 'Add a Heading text box in the reserved top space and type the headline.', 'Apply the headline_font/body_font pairing from Text > Effects.', 'Recolor accents using the color_palette HEX codes via the color picker.'). No generic advice ('be creative') — every step must be something the user can literally click.

criteria.question: Does the card faithfully and vividly capture the user's original concept?
Is magic_media_prompt concrete, renderable, and correctly ordered (subject->medium->composition->lighting->color->camera->quality) with no vague abstractions?
Are headline/subtext sharp and short, is color_palette valid coherent HEX, and is the font pairing + background layer distribution sound?
Are the action steps concrete, ordered, and literally clickable in Canva (not generic advice)?
Does the prompt use Canva-friendly library keywords AND reserve deliberate negative space for the typography layer?
Is the output 100% free of chat/question language, greetings, or meta-commentary — pure Canva automation data?

review_rubric.scale: 0-10 per criterion, weighted average determines final score. Any detected forbidden_chat_phrase caps format_discipline at 0 regardless of other scoring.
